subject: Data visualization at scale for edge case curation
text:
Hi [NAME],

Congratulations on the recent partnership with Dayton Airport - I'd imagine
this has increased the collection of in-field data once again?

We recently started working with Automotus, who also produce very similar
models to Metropolis (permit matching, car counting, etc.), and they had
problems with data visualization across hundreds of thousands of hours of
driving data. So I thought I'd reach out to see if you're encountering
similar challenges at Metropolis?

We enabled them, along with other mobility companies' AI teams (Woven by
Toyota, Metropolis, etc.), to curate data across hundreds of millions of
multimodal files (image, video), using metadata filtering, similarity
search, embedding visualization, etc. In turn, they were better able to
identify edge cases to annotate and iterate, and build more accurate models
faster.

Not sure how familiar you are with Encord - we're a data development
platform built for advanced computer vision and multimodal AI teams to
build better models (~5 years old, 100+ employees, and $50M+ in funding).

Would you be open to a quick intro call this week or next? I'm usually
pretty free Thursday/Friday mornings but happy to flex as needed.

subject: Automated Annotation for Hand Tracking and Object Detection
text:
Hi [NAME],

Congrats on being featured in Amazon's Industrial Innovation Fund spotlight
- great recognition.

I saw [COMPANY]'s post showcasing hand tracking, object detection, and 3D
fusion, and wondered if annotation has been a bottleneck as you've scaled?
Many teams we work w/ in the warehouse automation space (Ambi Robotics,
Pickle Robot etc) faced similar issues with in-house tooling slowing down
model iteration cycles.

We're now mostly assisting with improving their labelling efficiency
(autolabelling using SAM2, tracking algos, agentic integrations for
pre-labelling etc.) & overall pipeline integration (i.e. tightly coupled
data curation/annotation workflows).

Not sure how familiar you are with Encord - we're a data development
platform built for advanced computer vision and multimodal AI teams to
build better models (~5 years old, 70+ employees, and $50M+ in funding).

Would you be open to a 30-min chat with our team? We're pretty free
Thursday 26th, 9.30am - 11am or 10am to 2.30pm?

subject: Fast model iterations for quicker product development
text:
Hi [NAME],

Sorry we didn't get a chance to connect at CVPR. We caught up with Zippin
(partner to Encord) at our dinner we hosted there - they're working on
similar product detection CV models to Mashgin, focused on eliminating
checkout lines. So I wanted to reach out and see if you want to share
perspectives.

We've been helping them boost labelling efficiency (with SAM2, agentic
pre-labelling, etc.) and streamline their pipeline by tightly integrating
curation and annotation - freeing up engineers previously maintaining
non-core DataOps infra to focus on product development.

For context, Encord is an end-to-end ML DataOps platform for data
visualisation, curation, annotation, model eval - helping teams label data

Would you be open to a quick intro call? I'm free Weds/Thurs mornings (PT)
next week - happy to flex.

subject: [COMPANY] / Encord - Improving QA Workflows
text:
Hi [NAME],

I hope you had a nice weekend.

I'm part of the text & audio team at Encord and recently spoke with your
colleague Isaac Chung at ICLR. He highlighted a need for audio/text
transcription and speaker diarization, and mentioned that the team
currently uses LabelStudio.

Issac highlighted you as one of the people responsible for LabelStudio and
suggested we schedule some time to showcase why customers move from
LabelStudio to Encord when they need greater multimodal annotation control
and more robust quality assurance.

A few advantages worth highlighting:

   - A natively multimodal UI, i.e. we can annotate audio and text/PDF
   files natively (vs treating them like images)
   - Scalable QA workflows with detailed traceability and performance
   tracking (speed, quality, etc.)
   - The ability to route annotations to specific annotators or groups

I've provisionally put some time in your calendar for this Thursday morning
to discuss, but please feel free to suggest a better time if that doesn't
suit.

subject: Encord Intro - Helping teams like Nuro clean and curate driving data
text:
Hi [NAME],

I recently read that [COMPANY] has addressed over 200,000 safety scenarios -
an impressive stat that speaks to the scale and complexity of your ML
systems. We recently caught up with the AI team at Nuro at CVPR, who were
struggling with visualizing and curating 100s of hours of driving data, so
I thought it might be worth reaching out to see if you're facing similar
challenges at [COMPANY]?

We work w/ many autonomous vehicle/robotic AI teams (Woven by Toyota, Fox
Robotics etc) and enable them to curate data across hundreds of millions of
multimodal files (image, video, LiDAR, PCD, audio), using metadata
filtering, similarity search, embedding visualization, etc. This allows
them to better surface edge cases to improve perception, prediction, and
planning models.

For context… Encord is a end-to-end ML data ops platform for data
visualization, curation and annotation allowing team to label data 2x-10x
faster than in-house or first gen tools, resulting in shorter model
iteration cycles & improved model performance.

Would you be open to a quick intro call this week or next - I'm free this
Thursday/Friday mornings? Happy to flex as needed.

subject: Intro from Christoph Meyer
text:
Hi [NAME], hope you're keeping well.

By way of introduction, I'm part of the AV team at Encord and have been in
touch with Christoph, who suggested I reach out. For context, we've
recently started working with Woven by Toyota, Wayve, and Oxa - so I
thought it could be interesting to explore if we might be able to help at
McLaren / [COMPANY] in a similar way.

The common challenges these teams faced were with existing data
visualisation and curation solutions (typically internal tools) that lacked
the speed and scalability required to efficiently visualise their training
datasets - often struggling beyond ~1M frames. At Encord, we've built a
high-performance architecture that supports indexing and searching through
billions of multimodal data items, using embedding visualisations, quality
metric filters, and natural language searches. This helps AV teams avoid
bottlenecks in model development.

If this sounds interesting, I'd be happy to chat and share what we're
seeing work well for our other AV partners. Let me know if you'd be open to
a 20-minute chat later this week? Thursday or Friday is quite open for me
at the moment.
